newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold rally could extend to $346-$347.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold rally could extend to $346-$347.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Precious metals prices were forecast to continue Thursday's rally on Friday although the extent of the rise could be limited, technical analysts said.
Gold had the potential to reach resistance at $346.95 but concerted profit taking when New York opened could turn prices back.
GOLD
The market faces major technical resistance at $346.95-$347.00 assuming it gets through the less established resistance at $345.00 on Friday, technical analysts said.
Thursday's high of $345.15 was gold's highest bid since $346.10 on April 15.

The rally, driven by the weaker dollar and Wednesday's 140-point fall in the Down Jones industrial average advanced in thin trading yesterday when most of Europe was closed for the Ascension Day holiday.
"There is quite a lot of pessimism in the trading department this morning," one Europe-based market analyst said surveying Thursday's rally.
"But that may mean there is a good chance of it going higher," he added.
All the precious metals could benefit from further weakness in the value of U.S. dollar, especially against the yen where it hit a one-month low on Thursday.
It was around 123.08 on Friday morning, just above Thursday's 123.75 low amid foreign exchange market fears that central bank intervention was imminent.
"The technical support level is 121.60 and there must be a chance of it weakening to that and that must be good for the metals," the technical analyst said.
AT 0730 GMT gold was indicated at $344.35/$344.85, up about 70 cents from Thursday's London close.
SILVER
At $4.83/$4.85 silver was on the verge of testing significant technical resistance, analysts said.

It was also around the area dealers had indicated would be the point at which some of the market's shorts would consider covering as their view changed from ever downwards to upwards and a retest of $5.00.
"Silver could be setting up a test of the $4.90 technical resistance," one analyst said.
The longer term charts put silver in a $4.71-$5.25 channel and an attempt at the top end was possible if the funds decided to come in, the analyst added.
"It has a better chance than gold (of going higher). There is a real possibility of $5.00," he said.
At 0730 GMT silver was indicated at $4.83/$4.85, unchanged from Thursday's London close.
PLATINUM
The weaker dollar helped platinum prices to their highest levels since mid April.
Prices would remain volatile as long as the market was tight and lease rates for a month remained in double figures, analysts said.
The Russian-Japanese export talks stand off now in its sixth month was the major issue behind the market, analysts said.
The next techncial barrier for platinum was $385.00.
AT 0730 GMT platinum was indicated $381.75/$382.75, up $5.75 from Thursday's London close.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
